title: SLO-Gated CostPilot: phased batch/cache recommender with traffic shield
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Implement a conservative, SLO-first automation called CostPilot that: (1) analyzes live traffic to propose batching and KV-prefix caching configs, (2) applies changes in phased traffic-shielded rollouts, and (3) automatically rolls back on SLO regressions or anomaly signals. This ticket implements the core controller, the rollout policy hooks, anomaly detectors, and the observability dashboards required for safe automated applies.

Background and motivation:
- We currently have a manual checklist for batching/cache tuning; teams frequently under-apply conservative settings, leaving unit cost on the table.
- Previous automated attempts caused transient latency spikes when applied to bursty traffic shapes. We need SLO-aware automation that enforces latency and throughput guardrails and provides explicit traffic-shielding during experimentation.

Goals:
- Produce recommended batch and cache profiles for each model-endpoint based on online traffic shapes and historical latencies.
- Apply recommendations via staged rollouts that only increase configuration aggressiveness if SLOs are met.
- Detect regressions early with real-time anomaly detectors and revert to safe config automatically.
- Provide observability and playbook for on-call to understand and override decisions.

Non-goals:
- This work will not cover cost allocation/chargeback UI. It focuses on runtime config and safe automation flows.

Design summary:
1) Recommendation engine (CostPilot-suggest):
   - Inputs: token distribution, request size histogram, KV prefix hit ratios, per-model latency P50/P95/P99, and current batch sizes
   - Output: ranked candidate profiles {batch_size, max_window_ms, prefix_cache_ttl, kv_cache_mode} as strings with expected token-level savings and projected latency delta.
   - Conservative default: any candidate with projected P99 delta > +15ms is filtered out.

2) Rollout controller (traffic-shield):
   - Phased rollout: shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with dwell time and SLO checks at each step.
   - At each stage evaluate SLOs (latency P99, error rate, tail CPU), and anomaly detectors (traffic-shape drift, queue depth jumps).
   - If SLO breach or anomaly detected, immediate rollback to last known-good config and mark candidate "unsafe" for 24h.

3) Anomaly detection:
   - Lightweight online detectors: Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) on P99 deltas, burst-detection on RPS change > 50% in 1m, and queue-depth spike detector.
   - Composite rule: (EWMA_P99 > threshold) OR (burst_detect AND queue_depth_spike) triggers rollback.

4) Observability + alerts:
   - Dashboards: per-endpoint cost-savings projection, rollout stage, SLO health, and last-recommendation diff.
   - Alerts: Pager duty when automated rollback occurs or when a candidate is repeatedly unstable (3 fails in 7d).

Acceptance criteria:
- Recommendation engine provides ranked candidates with confidence scores and expected token savings for 90% of endpoints in Canary region.
- Rollout controller can perform staged apply and automatic rollback within <30s of anomaly detection.
- False positive rollback rate < 1% across canary traffic after 2 weeks of tuning.
- Observability dashboard surfaces per-endpoint recommendation details and a timeline of rollouts.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (canary): only apply to internal test endpoints and traffic-shadow in prod; enable auto-rollback. (2 weeks)
- Phase B (beta customers): opt-in endpoints for low-risk models (small seq len). (3 weeks)
- Phase C (gradual): opt-out default for other endpoints after metrics stable (4 weeks)

Safety knobs and limits:
- Never raise batch_size > 4x baseline in a single rollout stage.
- TTL for prefix cache increases limited to 5x baseline or 60s, whichever is smaller.
- Max concurrent automated rollouts globally: 30.
- SLO thresholds per endpoint are derived from current SLOs; defaults: P99_latency increase allowed: +12ms; error_rate delta allowed: +0.05%.

Testing strategy:
- Synthetic workload tests: replay traffic with burst scenarios and long-tail sequences.
- Chaos tests: simulate node CPU starvation to ensure rollbacks trigger.
- Staging e2e with canary pipeline and validation harness comparing control vs candidate.

Dependencies and related work:
- Requires runtime hooks for staged config apply (ENG-92017).
- Uses the safety gating primitives from protectorflow (ENG-53122).
- Needs updated latency profiling library (ENG-129321).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How conservative should confidence scoring be for cold-start endpoints? Proposal: require >48h of telemetry before auto-apply, otherwise proposal goes to manual review.
- Should we allow manual overrides to skip stages for high-trust customers? Proposal: Yes, via RBAC guard with audit log.

Documentation and runbook:
- Provide a runbook for on-call: how to inspect rollout, force rollback, and mark candidate as quarantined.
- Add docs: CostPilot recommendations overview, scoring model, and troubleshooting guide.

qa_checklist: Unit tests for recommendation scorer with mocked histograms
E2E staging run comparing control and candidate for 24h
Simulated burst test causing >50% RPS spike to validate rollback
postmortem_plan: If an automated rollout causes customer-impacting SLO regressions, trigger P0 incident process, capture timeline, revert all related changes, and disable auto-applies for 72h until root cause is addressed.
audit_log_notes: All automated applies will create a changelog entry containing: endpoint, previous_config, applied_config, actor=CostPilot, confidence_score, and audit_id. Audit entries stored for 365 days.
final_notes: Next steps: finish PR for rollout controller (blocking: add per-endpoint SLO thresholds API), wire up dashboard alerts, and schedule canary start on 2025-03-15.
